The Friars, led by fifth-year head coach [[Ed Cooley]], played their home games at the [[Dunkin' Donuts Center]], and were members of the [[Big East Conference]]. They finished the season 24–11, 10–8 in Big East play to finish in a tie for fourth place. They defeated [[2015–16 Butler Bulldogs men's basketball team|Butler]] in the quarterfinals of the [[2016 Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]] to advance to the semifinals where they lost to [[2015–16 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2016 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as a #9 seed where they defeated [[2015–16 USC Trojans men's basketball team|USC]] in the first round, then lost to [[2015–16 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] in the second round.{{cite news|url=https://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/article66816167.html|title=Bullock’s layup gives Providence 70-69 win over USC|first=Patrick|last=Stevens|work=[[The News & Observer]]|date=March 18, 2016|access-date=February 4, 2024}}{{cite news|url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/college/article67166552.html|title=UNC back in Sweet 16 after 85-66 win over Providence|first=Andrew|last=Carter|work=[[The Charlotte Observer]]|date=March 20, 2016|access-date=February 4, 2024}} == Previous season == The [[2014–15 Providence Friars men's basketball team|Friars]] finished the [[2014–15 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2014–15 season]] 22–12 overall and 11–7 in [[2014–15 Big East Conference men's basketball season|Big East play]] to finish in fourth place. They defeated [[2014–15 St. John's Red Storm men's basketball team|St. John's]] in the quarterfinals and lost to [[2014–15 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]] in the semifinals of the [[2015 Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]].
